title.narrative: Multitranche Financing Facility (MFF) - Rajasthan Urban Sector Development Investment Program (Tranche 1)

description.narrative: To increase economic growth, reduce poverty and sustain improvement in the urban environment and quality of life in the Jaisalmer, Alwar and Jhalawar/Jhalarapatan. The expected outcome of the Tranche 1 will be increased access to sustainable urban infrastructure and services for people in the Project ULBs, and improved capacities of, and sustainable management of urban services by the Project ULBs.

title.narrative: Reports and Recommendations of the President

description.narrative: Improved access to urban infrastructure and services of three ULBs to manage urban services

People benifitted by improved access to sanitation in 15 program ULBs. Progress/Status: 0.1 million people (24.7% of town population) in 2 of 3 tranche 1 ULBs (Alwar and Jaisalmer) provided with improved sewerage services. Data Source: Review Missions, Quarterly Progress Reports Actual value:

People benifitted by improved access to water supply in 15 program ULBs. Progress/Status: 520,000 people (94.9% population) benefitted by improved access to water supply in tranche 1 ULBs (Alwar, Jaisalmer and Jhalawar-Jhalarapatan). Data Source: Review Missions, Quarterly Progress Reports Actual value:

About 0.21 million people living in notified slums of Investment Program ULBs provided with improved basic urban services and living conditions. Progress/Status: About 66,705 people in identified slums in project 1 ULBs benefited with improved basic urban services and living conditions. Data Source: Review Missions, Quarterly Progress Reports Base year: 2007 Baseline value: N

All Investment Program ULBs with access to appropriate sanitary landfill facilities, and ULBs with capacity and facilities to collect municipal waste. Progress/Status: Sanitary landfills provided in project 1 ULBs but not functional. State government decided to develop compost plants by Rajasthan Awas Vikas Nigam. Data Source: Review Missions, Quarterly Progress Reports Base year: 2007 Baseline value: N

All ULBs with a population density of 150 households/hectare and water supply of 135 lpcd provided with sewerage facilities including STPs. Progress/Status: Project 1 ULBs are yet to achieve a population density of 150 households/ hectare. However, sewerage facilities have been provided in two of the project 1 ULBs (Alwar and Jaisalmer). Data Source: Review Missions, Quarterly Progress Reports Base year: 2007 Baseline value: N

Drainage outfalls provided in all Investment Program ULBs to reduce risks of flooding. Progress/Status: Flooding reduced in Jaisalmer, the only project 1 ULB where urban drainage works were undertaken. Data Source: Review Missions, Quarterly Progress Reports Base year: 2007 Baseline value: N

Improved traffic flow within the Investment Program ULBs and travel times between zones maintained at present levels or reduced in all the Investment Program ULBs. Progress/Status: Less than two minutes to cross the railway crossing as compared to earlier 5-15 minutes. Zero vehicle idling time for railway and road traffic has increased mobility, reduced average travel costs, and eliminated traffic congestion at the Itarna railway crossing in Alwar. Data Source: Review Missions, Quarterly Progress Reports Base year: 2007 Baseline value: N

Less wastewater discharged to water bodies. Progress/Status: 30 mld treatment capacity created for a 25-year design period. Current flow is about 5-6 mld. Data Source: Review Missions, Quarterly Progress Reports Base year: 2007 Baseline value: N
Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Improved solid waste management Indicator: Engineered municipal sanitary landfills and composting plants constructed according to Government of India's Municipal Solid Waste Management Rules, 2000, in all Investment Program ULBs. Progress/Status: Partly achieved. Sanitary landfills developed of 150 tons/day in Alwar, 35.7 tons/day in Jaisalmer, and 15.63 tons/day in Jhalawar. Data Source: Review Missions, Quarterly Progress report Actual value:

Output: Improvement in Water Supply in 3 project cities Indicator: District water quality testing laboratory in Jhalawar. Progress/Status: Achieved. Established and managed by public health engineering department. Data Source: Review Missions, Quarterly Project Reports Actual value:

Output: Improved social infrastructure Indicator: Major entry and exit roads, basic urban infrastructure, and amenities (e.g., water and sanitation, roads, streetlights, drainage, community hall, rainwater harvesting structures) developed for 0.21 million people living in identified slums in Investment Program ULBs. Progress/Status: Achieved. 66,705 people in identified slums in project 1 ULBs benefitted from basic urban infrastructure and amenities developed. Government order issued to provide basic municipal services to all the people living in slum areas, irrespective of land ownership. Data Source: Quarterly and annual progress reports Baseline year: 2007 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2007 Baseline value: N Target year: 2013 Target value: Y

Data Source: Review Missions, Quarterly Progress report Baseline year: 2007 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2007 Baseline value: N Target year: 2013 Target value: Y

Comprehensive traffic master plan for project 1 ULBs prepared. Data Source: Review Missions, Quarterly Progress Report Baseline year: 2007 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2007 Baseline value: N Target year: 2013 Target value: Y

Output: Improved urban transport Indicator: Identified transport infrastructure—roads over bridges or under bridges in Alwar, Baran and Chabra, Bharatpur, Bundi, Chittorgarh, Churu, Nagaur, Sawai Madhopur, and Sikar— completed in Investment Program ULBs. Progress/Status: Achieved. 2-lane road over bridge of 0.85 km constructed in Alwar. Data Source: Review Missions, Quarterly Progress Report Baseline year: 2007 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2007 Baseline value: N Target year: 2013 Target value: Y

Output: Improvement in Water Supply in 3 project cities Indicator: New distribution pipelines installed to increase piped water supply coverage to 90% of households in Investment Program ULBs. Progress/Status: Achieved. 228.1 km of distribution pipelines installed to increase piped water supply to more than 90% households in project 1 ULBs. Data Source: Review Missions, Quarterly Project Reports Baseline year: 2007 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2007 Baseline value: N Target year: 2013 Target value: Y

Output: Improvement in Water Supply in 3 project cities Indicator: Source augmentation and new treatment plants in Alwar, Jaisalmer, Baran-Chabra, Barmer, Rajsamand, Dhaulpur, Karauli, Churu, Nagaur, Sawai Madhopur, and Sikar. Progress/Status: Achieved. Source augmented and water treatment plants rehabilitated in project 1 ULBs. For water security, 15 days storage capacity at Mohangarh headworks created for the desert city of Jaisalmer. Data Source: Review Missions, Quarterly Project Reports Baseline year: 2007 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2007 Baseline value: N Target year: 2013 Target value: Y

Output: Improvement in Water Supply in 3 project cities Indicator: System rehabilitation and UFW reduction program implemented in all Investment Program ULBs, including replacement of excessively leaking carrier mains; repair and replacement of distribution mains; repair and replacement of leaking house connections older than 10 years installation or replacement of consumer water meters in all existing connections; refurbishment or replacement of old pumping machinery; installation of bulk meters at all supply points; rehabilitation of water treatment plants; augmentation of storage capacities; and provision of chlorination facilities. Progress/Status: Achieved. New water supply ring main of 28.15 km laid; 11 storage reservoirs constructed and 4 standalone chlorinators installed, 95 km water distribution pipeline rehabilitated or replaced in Alwar. New intake and supply augmentation, including 57.1 km of transmission mains, 3 storage reservoir and power supply line completed in Jaisalmer. As planned, the clear water reservoir was replaced with 7.7 km of rising main, based on design considerations. 2 intake works and 2 clear water reservoirs rehabilitated, 9 storage reservoirs constructed, 14.8 km of rising mains laid and 2 water treatment plants at Jhalawar and Jhalarapatan rehabilitated. 154 bulk flow meters and 48 electromagnetic flow meters (in Alwar) and 32,456 household water meters installed in the project 1 ULBs. Rehabilitation of pumping machinery at 59 tube wells and 19 pump houses, provision of 69 submersible pumps and provision of feeder panels at 107 tube wells undertaken at Alwar. In Jaisalmer, 2 pump houses constructed and pumping machinery installed. In Jhalawar-Jhalarapatan, 2 centrifugal pumps installed at intake works. Data Source: Review Missions, Quarterly Project Reports Baseline year: 2007 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2007 Baseline value: N Target year: 2013 Target value: Y

Output: Improvement in sewerage and sanitation Indicator: Sewerage system—outfall, trunk sewers, and tertiary networks and household connections in priority areas as identified—and sewage treatment plants (STPs) constructed in Alwar (STP capacity 20 mld), Jaisalmer (10 mld), Baran (12 mld), Chabra (4 mld), Bharatpur (20 mld), Bundi (10 mld), Chittorgarh (10 mld), Dhaulpur (10 mld), Karauli (8 mld), Churu (15 mld), Nagaur (10 mld), Sawai Madhopur (13 mld), and Sikar (16 mld). Progress/Status: Achieved. 30 mld treatment capacity achieved with 20 mld and 10 mld STPs at Alwar and Jaisalmer, respectively. 17.5 km of outfall, 20.8 km of trunk sewers and 53.8 km of laterals and 1,410 household connections completed in Alwar. 7.7 km of outfall, 2.3 km of trunk sewers and 44.0 km of laterals and 880 household connections completed in Jaisalmer. Data Source: Review Missions, Quarterly Progress Report Baseline year: 2007 Baseline value: Y Baseline year: 2007 Baseline value: Y Target year: 2013 Target value: N
